what_was_done: Three changes in commits.py _flush_locked. (1) The `git diff --cached --name-only -z` that builds commit_rels now runs with --no-renames, so a delete-plus-add pair of a renamed state file lists both its paths and the deletion is committed together with the addition; before, rename detection printed only the new name, the staged deletion rode on, and every later flush failed on `git add -A -- <gone path>` ('pathspec did not match any files'). (2) Staging splits the valid rels: paths still in the worktree stage with `git add -A --`, paths gone from the worktree with `git rm --cached -q --ignore-unmatch --` (the same 40-path chunks), so a deletion already in the index — staged by a killed flush or by an earlier flush — no longer refuses. (3) The changed set also unions _staged_paths(root), the index's own leftovers read as `git diff --cached --name-only --no-renames -z` before staging: a staged rename is one 'R' record in status, which both changed_paths and _deleted_paths pass over, so a killed flush's staged rename would sit committed-never while flush reported 'clean'. Audit of every other git command in commits.py for rename, deletion, space, non-ASCII and already-staged: status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall and the two diffs are NUL-separated and never C-quoted, so spaces and non-ASCII come back whole (a rename pair in status is consumed and covered by the staged-diff union); add/rm --cached and commit --only take the paths as argv members, no shell; config user.email, rev-parse, merge-base take no paths. Tests (test_state_commits.py): test_flush_commits_a_renamed_story is the finding's probe — the second flush is 'committed' with both S-1.01.md and S-1.02.md in files, the tree is clean and the next flush clean; test_flush_commits_a_deletion_already_staged; test_flush_commits_a_rename_a_killed_flush_staged (status shows 'R ' and flush still commits both paths); test_flush_commits_a_renamed_name_with_space_and_accents runs a decision packet named 'nächste Runde.md' through status, staging, the diff and the commit pathspec. Each test was shown to fail against its reverted fix in a scratch copy of the tree.

locks.lock_release: an entry whose run_end cannot take flush.lock within the wait budget is still kept and lock.json is written with the kept entries (lock.json and the run records agree), and after the file lock is freed the call raises StoreBusy whose `released` attribute carries the entries that were released — busy is no longer silent and the plan line 'StoreBusy after wait, which bounds the whole call' holds again. Caller note: `lock_release` must now be caught for StoreBusy; exc.released holds the entries actually released. cmd_lock._run wraps both the --force and the selector path: a StoreBusy returns exit 1 with `released` as far as it got, `holder` set to a kept entry (never null) and an error that says a flush is running and to retry — distinct from the 'another session's live run holds the lock' message. Tests: test_lock_release_wait_bounds_the_whole_call (test_state_locks.py) now expects StoreBusy within 1.0 s at wait=0.5 with lock.json unchanged and the run still live; new test_cmd_lock_release_while_a_flush_holds_the_lock (test_state_cmds.py) asserts `vsdd lock release --force` exits 1, holder is the kept live entry, the error names the flush, lock.json keeps its entry and its run, and the same command succeeds once the flush.lock holder dies. Both fail against the reverted behaviour (verified in a scratch copy).

The evidence order is now total and independent of the clock's whole-second stamp. gate_evidence.evidence_write stamps `seq` on the record under flush.lock (EVIDENCE_LOCK_WAIT = 2.0 s; StoreBusy if not had): one more than the highest seq in the subject's directory (_next_seq), so a rewrite renumbers above everything there and two records of one second order by the write's order, never the file name. _evidence_records sorts by (seq, at, file name); every lookup that reads 'the latest record' inherits the order; `at` stays for people. evidence-record.schema.json gains a required integer `seq` (minimum 1) and the `at` description now says the lookup orders by seq; the three fixtures (valid_red, valid_green, invalid_missing-at) carry seq, so the invalid fixture still fails for exactly its stated reason. tools/build.py --check reports all generated copies current (evidence-record is a NON_PRELUDE schema; no generated literal carries it). rewrite/spec/records/evidence.md states the seq rule with the finding id. Test test_same_second_records_order_by_write writes two same-second red records whose file names sort against the write order and asserts the records come back in write order with ascending seqs, then asserts a rewrite moves its record last; reverting the sort to (at, name) in a scratch copy fails it.

The per-kind record check in flush is now a table, commits.record_kinds(): one row per tracked record kind — cycle-record (cycles/**/cycle.json, schema, no cap), closure-record (cycles/*/units/*.json, schema plus CLOSURE_CAP), decision-record (cycles/*/decisions/*.json, schema plus RECORD_CAP), decision-packet (cycles/*/decisions/*.md, PACKET_CAP), notes (notes.json, parse only) — each row carrying kind, claim(path), schema, cap and parse. _record_problem judges through the claiming row and returns None when no row claims the file; _flush_locked turns that into a `no_validator` refusal naming the file, for every changed file under the record folders (the cycles tree and notes.json), so a tracked record kind added later cannot be committed unchecked and nothing fails quietly when a kind is missing. rewrite/spec/topics/state-commits.md step 3 now says a new tracked record kind must register its validator in that table in the same step as it first lands in the state tree. Tests (test_state_commits.py): test_flush_refuses_an_unclaimed_record_file (a stray .factory/cycles/product-1/extra/stray.json is rejected, named with no_validator, and never committed, while a valid notes.json in the same flush commits; the flush is partial and not ok) and test_record_kinds_cover_the_shipped_tracked_records (every record schema the unit ships for a tracked record — cycle-record, closure-record, decision-record — has a row, each row claims its own path form, and every row names a shipped schema). Disabling the refusal in a scratch copy fails the first test.
